title: Geometry of the affinization map under first-cohomology vanishing
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: every open covering has a finite subcover and its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Quasi-coherent modules are on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and $H^q$ is the right derived functor of global sections of the underlying additive sheaf [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Assume $H^1(X,F)=0$ for every quasi-coherent module $F$. Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Absolute means over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: regard $X$ as an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ through $X\to S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with the same etale scheme charts, point space and small etale ringed site. In this sense, and with algebraic spaces and morphisms below taken over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, there is a unique absolute morphism $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ inducing the identity of $A$ on global functions. Its diagonal $X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}X$ is a closed immersion on every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Moreover $p$ is universally injective: for every algebraic space $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, the induced map $|X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}T|\to|T|$ is injective, using the field-valued point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The same charts and ringed small etale site preserve the quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness and H1 hypothesis. Work over $\mathbf Z$ henceforth. Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-target-global-functions] to $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $1_A$. Its bijection gives exactly one $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ inducing $1_A$.

proof.text: For a field $K$ and a map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, let $Z=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}K$. By [lem-sfb-space-h1-vanishing-affine-base-change], $Z$ is qcqs, its diagonal over $K$ is quasi-compact, $H^1(Z,G)=0$ for all quasi-coherent $G$, and its structural map identifies $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ with $K$ as a $K$-algebra. These are valid for every field map, including non-flat $A\to K$.

source.place: Tag 07V4 first paragraph; Tag 07V0 affine base change.

proof.text: By (2) and (3) of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] for $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, regard $Z$ with its structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ as an algebraic space over $K$, with the same scheme charts, point space and small etale ringed site; $Z(K)$ denotes its $K$-morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$. For $x,x\prime\in Z(K)$, [lem-sfb-qs-space-rational-point-topology] says their images are closed singletons and that distinct morphisms have distinct images. If they were distinct, [lem-sfb-space-h1-separate-disjoint-closed] would give $a$ evaluating to $0$ at $x$ and to $1$ at $x\prime$. But $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=K$ as a $K$-algebra, so evaluation at either $K$-point is the identity on $K$, contradicting $0\ne1$. Thus every fibre has at most one $K$-point. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-universal-injectivity-criteria], (3) implies (1), to $p$, viewing algebraic spaces as stacks with discrete groupoids. For any algebraically closed $K$, two $K$-points over the same point of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ are two $K$-points of the fibre just treated and hence equal; all isomorphisms in these discrete groupoids are identities. The criterion gives injectivity after every stack base change, in particular after every algebraic-space base change required here.

source.place: Tag 07V4 closed-rational-point argument with Tag 07V1 and decent-spaces.tex Tag 07U5; equivalent field-valued-point criterion stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 0CPN.

proof.text: Choose a scheme $Y$ and a surjective integral $f:Y\to X$ using [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-integral-scheme-cover]. By [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence], $f$ is affine and $Y$ is qcqs. Apply part (1) of [lem-sfb-space-h1-vanishing-affine-base-change] to conclude $H^1(Y,G)=0$ for every quasi-coherent module on its small etale site.

source.place: Tag 07V5 first paragraph, using decent-spaces.tex Tag 09YB and Tag 07V0(1).

proof.text: For every quasi-coherent Zariski ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$, [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] gives its associated quasi-coherent small etale module. By [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison], $H^1(Y,I)$ on the Zariski site equals its etale cohomology and is zero by the preceding step. Since $Y$ is a quasi-compact scheme, [lem-pqf-quasicompact-h1-zero] now implies $Y$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 07V5 application of coherent.tex Tag 01XF (lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering); comparison descent.tex Tags 03DX and 03DW.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], the structure morphism $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated, since $Y$ is affine. The sheaf fibre product $Y\times_{\mathbf Z}Y$ is represented by the scheme product, so by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] every scheme-test pullback of the scheme closed immersion $\Delta_Y$ is a closed immersion; thus the absolute diagonal of $Y$ is a closed immersion in the representable sense. By [lem-sfb-space-integral-universally-closed], the integral surjection $f:Y\to X$ is universally closed. Apply [lem-sfb-space-uc-surjection-separation] to obtain that the absolute diagonal $\Delta_X:X\to X\times_{\mathbf Z}X$ is a closed immersion on every scheme test.

source.place: Tag 07V5 final paragraph: Tags 0415 and 05Z2(2); affine-source separatedness schemes.tex Tags 01KN and 01KV.

proof.text: The square with top $1_X:X\to X$, bottom $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}X\to X\times_{\mathbf Z}X$, left $\Delta_p$ and right $\Delta_X$ is Cartesian: a pair with equal images under $p$ lies on either diagonal exactly when its two entries agree. For any scheme test $T\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}X$, the pullback of $\Delta_p$ is therefore the pullback of $\Delta_X$ by the composite $T\to X\times_{\mathbf Z}X$. This is a closed immersion by the preceding step. Thus $p$ is separated on all scheme tests. The unique construction and universal injectivity were proved in steps 1 and 3.

source.place: Tag 07V5 conclusion, spelled out using the defining scheme tests of a representable closed immersion.

lean.statement: theorem space_acyclic_affinization_geometry {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) [HasSheafify X.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u}] [HasExt.{u + 1} (Sheaf X.etaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u})] (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X) (hH : ∀ (F : X.Modules) (_ : F.IsQuasicoherent), Subsingleton (Sheaf.H ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf X.structureSheaf).obj F) 1)) : ∃ (A : CommRingCat.{u}) (π : (Functor.const (acyclicAffinizationAbsoluteSpace X).EtaleSiteᵒᵖ).obj A ⟶ (acyclicAffinizationAbsoluteSpace X).etaleForget.op ⋙ Scheme.Γ), Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk A π)) ∧ ∃ p : acyclicAffinizationAbsoluteSpace X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (specULiftZIsTerminal.from (Spec A))), (∀ T : (acyclicAffinizationAbsoluteSpace X).EtaleSite, π.app (op T) = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso A).inv ≫ (yoneda.preimage (T.obj.hom ≫ p.hom.hom)).left.appTop) ∧ (∀ q : acyclicAffinizationAbsoluteSpace X ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (specULiftZIsTerminal.from (Spec A))), (∀ T : (acyclicAffinizationAbsoluteSpace X).EtaleSite, π.app (op T) = (Scheme.ΓSpecIso A).inv ≫ (yoneda.preimage (T.obj.hom ≫ q.hom.hom)).left.appTop) → q = p) ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ f ↦ IsClosedImmersion f.left) (pullback.diagonal p.hom.hom) ∧ ∀ (T : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (g : T ⟶ schemeSpace (Over.mk (specULiftZIsTerminal.from (Spec A)))), Function.Injective (mapPoint (pullback.snd p.hom g.hom).hom)
